priorFindingsResolution.status: REGRESSED -- the concurrent-racer TOCTOU is closed, but a new, more severe permanent-lockout defect was introduced
priorFindingsResolution.note: Verified the owner-file-write + sleep 0.2 + re-read (healthcheck-lib.sh:43-44) does correctly resolve the specific double-run race described in the round-4 verdict: mkdir is atomic, so exactly one racer's mkdir call can create the directory at any given instant, and the owner re-check + deferred trap installation (trap set only AFTER the ownership check passes, at line 45) ensures a losing racer bails at line 44 without ever installing a cleanup trap that could delete the winner's lock. That specific safety property (mkdir atomic + loser gets return 0) now holds. HOWEVER, writing 'owner' inside LOCK_DIR makes the directory non-empty for as long as it is held, which breaks the plain `rmdir` used in the STALE-lock steal path (line 37): rmdir only succeeds on an empty directory. If a healthcheck run is abnormally killed (SIGKILL / sleep-wake reap / OOM) AFTER acquiring the lock but before its RETURN trap fires -- exactly the FIND-013 scenario this same lock exists to recover from, per the code's own comment at lines 31-32 -- the leftover non-empty lock directory can NEVER be stolen again: rmdir fails silently (ENOTEMPTY, swallowed), mkdir then fails (EEXIST), and `|| return 0` fires with ZERO log output. This permanently and silently disables ALL healthcheck functions (dead-session restart, stuck-prompt restart, staleness restart, output-stale self-fix escalation) for that loop. See FIND-026 for full reproduction trace.

finalAssessment.summary: FIND-025 (the loop-name namespace split) is genuinely and fully resolved -- confirmed by tracing every call site plus a whole-tree grep for the marker-file naming pattern; this is a real, positive fix. FIND-023 and FIND-020, however, were each 'fixed' by trading the originally-reported failure mode for a different, and in FIND-020's case more severe, failure mode: (1) the owner-file mechanism added to close FIND-020's concurrent-racer race makes the lock directory non-empty, which breaks the plain-rmdir stale-lock-steal recovery this SAME lock depends on for resilience against abnormal termination (a scenario the code's own adjacent comment explicitly says must not happen) -- one hard-kill silently and permanently disables all self-heal functions for that loop, with no log trace; (2) the pane-liveness check added to close FIND-023's wall-clock-kill-of-real-work concern cannot distinguish genuine progress from a genuinely deadlocked/hung tool call, both of which show the identical 'esc to interrupt' footer -- so the entire 180-minute ceiling is now inert against the single most likely hang mode (a stuck network/browser call) for a fixer whose job is explicitly heavy browser/network automation. Neither of these two re-patched mechanisms has ANY automated test coverage, so both defects would have gone undetected by a green test run and can silently recur on any future edit. Given a critical-severity, code-verifiable, disk-traceable defect (FIND-026) that directly contradicts the CLAIM's core 'self-heal ... no babysitting' promise, overall verdict is FAIL.
